metadata.title: Midjourney, Part Two.
metadata.audience: HAI Lyrical Literacy volunteers who have completed Part 1. Internal training, not promotion.
metadata.narration_notes: Host is Rohan V. Full name spoken EXACTLY ONCE, in BOUT. Phonetic spellings are deliberate for Kokoro G2P: 'Rohaan' = Row-Haan. Do NOT 'correct' them. SPINE: Midjourney's own seven prompt elements from Prompt Basics (Subject/Medium/Environment/Lighting/Color/Mood/Composition), in the vendor's order. Not my segmentation. WORKED EXAMPLE: a real prompt transcribed from 'Create Tab.png'. B07 corrects its plain-text negation against the docs, with attribution, and does NOT claim the images failed. No version numbers. No pricing. No series count. Every MjL2* scene passes kicker='LYRICAL LITERACY · MIDJOURNEY TUTORIAL PART 2'. Heteronym pass: avoid 'live', 'read' as past tense, 'close', 'record', 'present', 'content', 'separate' as adjective. Note 'read it against the seven' in B06 is imperative present - fine. '--no' is spoken as 'two dashes, then the word no' because Kokoro cannot voice the glyphs.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Rohaan from Humanitarians AI. This is Part 2. In Part 1 you typed something into the bar and got four images back. This one is about the typing. Midjourney publishes a list of what a prompt should answer, and it is shorter than you would expect.

show.event: Composer fades up under the serif greeting
Send arms terracotta; running indicator appears

props.command: What actually belongs in a Midjourney prompt?
output: Seven elements - Midjourney's own list, not a technique.
A real prompt from this workspace, read against all seven.
And the one thing that prompt gets wrong.

beats.narration_text: Seven questions. That is Midjourney's own list, out of their documentation. Subject, medium, environment, lighting, colour, mood, composition. You do not have to answer all seven every time, and a one word prompt still works. But when an image comes back wrong, it is almost always because one of these was left for the model to guess.

show.event: Seven cards land together, all equal weight
The closing line resolves beneath them

props.title: Seven questions
props.closing: You are not writing a sentence. You are answering a list.

beats.narration_text: Subject is who or what. A person, an animal, a character, a location. It is the one thing you cannot leave out. Medium is what form it takes: a photo, a painting, an illustration, a sculpture. The prompt coming up answers medium twice, once as a character design and once as an animated film look.

show.event: Grid lands; Subject and Medium hold full colour, rest desaturate

props.title: Subject, then medium
props.sparkLine: What it is. What form it takes.

beats.narration_text: Environment is where it is. Indoors, outdoors, underwater, in the city. Lighting is what kind: soft, ambient, overcast, neon, studio. Both are easy to skip and both change everything. A plain grey studio background is not a missing answer. It is a decision to keep the background quiet so the subject carries the frame.

show.event: Grid lands; Environment and Lighting hold

props.title: Where it is, and how it is lit
props.sparkLine: A quiet background is still a choice.

beats.narration_text: Colour asks in what shades. Vibrant, muted, monochromatic, pastel. Name the colours rather than the feeling: charcoal grey is a decision, scary colours is not. Mood is the feeling to evoke, and the prompt in this workspace has the sharpest version of it. Threatening, but suitable for a family friendly adventure.

show.event: Grid lands; Color and Mood hold

props.title: Colour, then mood
props.sparkLine: Name the shade, not the vibe.

beats.narration_text: Composition is how it is framed. Portrait, headshot, closeup, birds eye view. This is the one that saves the most reruns, because it is where you say what must not be cropped. The workspace prompt asks for a three quarter front view with the whole animal in frame, tail and paws included. It reads as fussy right up until a character comes back with its feet cropped.

props.title: How it is framed
props.sparkLine: Say what must not be cropped.

beats.narration_text: Here is a prompt from this workspace, written for a character set rather than from a checklist. Check it against the seven and every one is there. Subject, medium, environment, lighting, colour, mood, composition. Being specific and answering the list turn out to be the same thing.

show.event: The prompt lands in full on the left
The seven begin ticking off on the right

props.title: All seven, in one real prompt

beats.narration_text: One thing that prompt gets wrong. It ends with six exclusions written straight into the sentence. Midjourney's documentation is direct about this: describe what you do want, not what you do not. Mention a party with no cake and you may still get a cake. For exclusions use the parameter. Two dashes, then no. And keep each item to a single idea, because every word after it is taken on its own.

show.event: The real prompt's exclusion tail, quoted
The word splitting trap, full width

beats.narration_text: To review. Seven questions: subject, medium, environment, lighting, colour, mood, composition. Answer the ones that matter for the image you need. Name colours, not feelings. Say what must not be cropped. And to leave something out, reach for the parameter instead of writing the word no into your sentence.

artifactLines: Subject - who or what. The one element you cannot leave out.
Medium - photo, painting, illustration, sculpture, character design.
Environment - where it is. A plain backdrop is still a decision.
Lighting - soft, ambient, overcast, neon, studio.
Color - name the shade, not the feeling.
Mood - the feeling to evoke, and how far it may go.
Composition - how it is framed, and what must not be cropped.
Exclusions - use the parameter, not the word 'no' in the sentence.

beats.narration_text: Part 3 opens one image properly. The panel of actions beside it, where you vary, upscale, rerun, and turn a still into video. Bring a prompt you actually like. It is a better thing to work from.

Vary and Upscale, and what each pair of buttons does.
The three actions hidden until you switch them on - and Animate.
